case.question: How should delivery strategy differ between Dubai and Abu Dhabi?
expected: City-specific evidence or honest limits on differentiation

answer.headline: Provisional delivery plan: treat delivery and Abu Dhabi as validation phases first; build a fixed-cost own-rider zone in Dubai only after measured radius tests, and keep platform and own-rider options in both cities.

items.text: Deliveroo, a UAE-wide platform, describes two distinct UAE partner models: a platform-rider network with customer pickup, and Marketplace+ where restaurant staff deliver within a selectable area, minimum spend and delivery fee, with an option to request a platform rider. Both are described UAE-wide, not as city-specific, so channel choice is a testable configuration rather than a supported Dubai-versus-Abu Dhabi difference.

Curated evidence shows delivery-active sandwich/pizza-relevant operators in both cities: Allo Beirut lists a Hessa Street (Al Barsha) Dubai branch advertising delivery until 4 AM, and Talabat lists Operation Falafel in Madinat Khalifa A, Abu Dhabi with sandwich and shawarma categories. These are listings only; neither establishes order volume, catchment, or delivery saturation.

Gap: no curated or searched evidence establishes Dubai-versus-Abu Dhabi differences in delivery commissions, fees, rider availability, delivery radius, order density, or overnight demand. Treat any city-level delivery difference as unknown until measured; the platform own-rider/minimum-spend levers are the supported dials, not city-level facts.

Proposal: launch Dubai on platform-rider channels plus pickup (both described as Deliveroo UAE options), keep own-rider delivery off in month 1-2, and add Marketplace+-style own-rider delivery only for one defined zone once measured order density justifies the shift cost. Selectable delivery area and minimum spend are platform-documented levers, not chosen radii.

Proposal: test a late-evening and post-midnight Dubai window in the Hessa Street/Al Barsha operating environment, where a listed operator advertises delivery until 4 AM. Measure orders, prep load and rider wait per hour before extending hours; the advertised 4 AM window does not establish demand.

Proposal: apply sealed containers, hot/cold separation into insulated secondary units, and 60 C hot / 5 C cold / -18 C frozen holding to Dubai deliveries, per Dubai Municipality guidance. That guidance is version 2 issued 2023-08-31 and flagged needs_review, so confirm current amendments and activity-specific applicability before procurement.

sections.title: Proposed Abu Dhabi delivery play and shared mechanics

items.text: Proposal: run Abu Dhabi first on platform-rider channels plus pickup, mirroring the Dubai launch configuration, in a Khalifa City/Madinat Khalifa-type area where a sandwich and shawarma operator is listed on Talabat. Selectability of delivery area and minimum spend is the documented lever; the correct catchment there is unverified.

Proposal: in both cities, keep kebab sandwiches as the fast-moving delivery SKU and structure pizza for insulated transport; run a matched radius test (e.g. 3 km vs 5 km, same menu and pricing) per city and per channel, recording order frequency, prep-to-pickup time and packaging leakage rather than assuming a radius.

Proposal: use platform order tracking and rider-arrival alerts (described as UAE Deliveroo features) plus a hot-bag handover check in both cities, and quote all launch channels with the platform before committing to any own-rider zone or commission-dependent expansion.

assumptions: User profile: Jordanian-origin restaurant (assumption), core products meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches (assumption), target cities Dubai and Abu Dhabi (assumption); startup budget, rent budget, branch format, audience, positioning and opening date are unset.
Assumption: one production kitchen per city serving delivery, no existing rider fleet or platform contracts, and the same menu and price list used in both cities.
next_steps: Request written platform quotes for each city and each model (platform rider vs own rider / Marketplace+-style), listing commission basis, fixed fees, delivery radius, delivery fee and minimum spend before building a numeric delivery model.
Run a two-week per-city measurement grid: order counts by 2-hour band, prep time, rider wait, failed/completed deliveries, packaging leaks and repeat rate at two candidate radii.
Determine cold-chain and delivery-vehicle requirements for each emirate and confirm the current version of the Dubai Municipality food-transport guidance before specifying bags and vehicles.

Once per-order revenue, food, packaging, other variable costs, delivery share, commission rate, monthly fixed costs and operating days are all known or sourced, ask for the delivery unit-economics calculation; do not treat the current plan as a profitability forecast.

Provisional delivery plan: treat delivery and Abu Dhabi as validation phases first; build a fixed-cost own-rider zone in Dubai only after measured radius tests, and keep platform and own-rider options in both cities.

**Evidence base and city differentiation**

- **Fact:** Deliveroo, a UAE-wide platform, describes two distinct UAE partner models: a platform-rider network with customer pickup, and Marketplace+ where restaurant staff deliver within a selectable area, minimum spend and delivery fee, with an option to request a platform rider. Both are described UAE-wide, not as city-specific, so channel choice is a testable configuration rather than a supported Dubai-versus-Abu Dhabi difference. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/delivery>) [2](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/marketplace>)
- **Fact:** Curated evidence shows delivery-active sandwich/pizza-relevant operators in both cities: Allo Beirut lists a Hessa Street \(Al Barsha\) Dubai branch advertising delivery until 4 AM, and Talabat lists Operation Falafel in Madinat Khalifa A, Abu Dhabi with sandwich and shawarma categories. These are listings only; neither establishes order volume, catchment, or delivery saturation. [3](<https://www.allobeirutstreetfood.com/locations>) [4](<https://www.talabat.com/uae/restaurant/704423/operation-falafel-khalifa-city--ad-7?aid=1483>)
- **Fact:** Gap: no curated or searched evidence establishes Dubai-versus-Abu Dhabi differences in delivery commissions, fees, rider availability, delivery radius, order density, or overnight demand. Treat any city-level delivery difference as unknown until measured; the platform own-rider/minimum-spend levers are the supported dials, not city-level facts. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/delivery>) [2](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/marketplace>)

**Proposed Dubai delivery play**

- **Proposal:** Proposal: launch Dubai on platform-rider channels plus pickup \(both described as Deliveroo UAE options\), keep own-rider delivery off in month 1-2, and add Marketplace+-style own-rider delivery only for one defined zone once measured order density justifies the shift cost. Selectable delivery area and minimum spend are platform-documented levers, not chosen radii. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/delivery>) [2](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/marketplace>)
- **Proposal:** Proposal: test a late-evening and post-midnight Dubai window in the Hessa Street/Al Barsha operating environment, where a listed operator advertises delivery until 4 AM. Measure orders, prep load and rider wait per hour before extending hours; the advertised 4 AM window does not establish demand. [3](<https://www.allobeirutstreetfood.com/locations>)
- **Proposal:** Proposal: apply sealed containers, hot/cold separation into insulated secondary units, and 60 C hot / 5 C cold / -18 C frozen holding to Dubai deliveries, per Dubai Municipality guidance. That guidance is version 2 issued 2023-08-31 and flagged needs\_review, so confirm current amendments and activity-specific applicability before procurement. [5](<https://dmpmedia.dm.gov.ae/uploads/2024/02/2.-DM-FSD-GU63-Requirements-for-food-transportation-and-delivery-vehicles-guidelines-update.pdf>)

**Proposed Abu Dhabi delivery play and shared mechanics**

- **Proposal:** Proposal: run Abu Dhabi first on platform-rider channels plus pickup, mirroring the Dubai launch configuration, in a Khalifa City/Madinat Khalifa-type area where a sandwich and shawarma operator is listed on Talabat. Selectability of delivery area and minimum spend is the documented lever; the correct catchment there is unverified. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/delivery>) [2](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/marketplace>) [4](<https://www.talabat.com/uae/restaurant/704423/operation-falafel-khalifa-city--ad-7?aid=1483>)
- **Proposal:** Proposal: in both cities, keep kebab sandwiches as the fast-moving delivery SKU and structure pizza for insulated transport; run a matched radius test \(e.g. 3 km vs 5 km, same menu and pricing\) per city and per channel, recording order frequency, prep-to-pickup time and packaging leakage rather than assuming a radius.
- **Proposal:** Proposal: use platform order tracking and rider-arrival alerts \(described as UAE Deliveroo features\) plus a hot-bag handover check in both cities, and quote all launch channels with the platform before committing to any own-rider zone or commission-dependent expansion. [1](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/delivery>) [2](<https://merchants.deliveroo.com/en-AE/what-we-offer/marketplace>)

**Assumptions and limitations**

- User profile: Jordanian-origin restaurant \(assumption\), core products meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches \(assumption\), target cities Dubai and Abu Dhabi \(assumption\); startup budget, rent budget, branch format, audience, positioning and opening date are unset.
- Assumption: one production kitchen per city serving delivery, no existing rider fleet or platform contracts, and the same menu and price list used in both cities.

**Next steps**

- Request written platform quotes for each city and each model \(platform rider vs own rider / Marketplace+-style\), listing commission basis, fixed fees, delivery radius, delivery fee and minimum spend before building a numeric delivery model.
- Run a two-week per-city measurement grid: order counts by 2-hour band, prep time, rider wait, failed/completed deliveries, packaging leaks and repeat rate at two candidate radii.
- Determine cold-chain and delivery-vehicle requirements for each emirate and confirm the current version of the Dubai Municipality food-transport guidance before specifying bags and vehicles.
- Once per-order revenue, food, packaging, other variable costs, delivery share, commission rate, monthly fixed costs and operating days are all known or sourced, ask for the delivery unit-economics calculation; do not treat the current plan as a profitability forecast.
